name: Skymarcher Aspirant
oracle_text:
Ascend (If you control ten or more permanents, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game.)
This creature has flying as long as you have the city's blessing.
blocked_sentences: Ascend (If you control ten or more permanents, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game.)
This creature has flying as long as you have the city's blessing.

Scope: both printed lines are blocked, and the second is blocked twice over -- once because there is nothing to ask about (no city's blessing exists to be read) and once because a static's `condition` may not ask it even if it did. The card already in the hand-written pool (`data/cards/edgar.cards.json`) carries the correct printed `oracle_text` but implements neither line; it is a vanilla 2/1 Vampire Soldier, and `tests/cards/precon_deficits.json` records exactly that residual. No partial answer is possible: printing `"keywords": ["flying"]` unconditionally would be a strictly better card than the one printed (a 2/1 flier for {W} that flies from turn one regardless of board), and it would still leave the Ascend line unclaimed by any ability.

needs.what: the city's blessing as a per-player, one-way, permanent designation (rule 702.131 / 700.6): a field on `PlayerState` such as `has_city_s_blessing: bool`, set the moment its controller controls ten or more permanents and never unset -- it survives the permanents leaving, survives the source of the Ascend ability leaving the battlefield, and is shared by every card that player controls, so a second Ascend card printed later reads the blessing that a first card granted. Needs three parts: (a) the player-state field itself; (b) the continuous check, which is a STATE TRIGGER, not a triggered ability -- it is checked whenever state-based actions are, uses no stack and cannot be responded to, so it belongs in the state-based-action pass in `engine/` next to the existing legend-rule/lethal-damage checks, gated on the controller of a permanent (or resolving spell) with the Ascend ability; and (c) card-level vocabulary to say the permanent has Ascend at all -- most plausibly a card field like `"ascend": true`, since it is a one-word keyword ability with no parameters, and since making it a `Keyword` enum member would wrongly put it in the derived keyword list that `grant_keyword` and evasion checks read
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `PlayerState` (`src/automtg/engine/player.py:20-65`) stores life, zones, mana, land drops, commander tax/damage, loss and UI flags -- there is no general per-player flag, designation or counter of any kind, so the blessing has nowhere to live and no value expression or condition can read it back. The closest one-way flag in the engine is `monstrous` (`engine/objects.py:46-48`, set by the `monstrosity` op at `effects/ops_board.py:252`), and it is wrong in all three respects that matter here: it lives on an OBJECT, so it is cleared by `reset_permanent_state` on any zone change and cannot be shared between two cards; it is set by an op resolving from the stack rather than by a continuous check; and there is no op-driven route to a player-wide equivalent, because none of the 46 ops writes durable player state. Nor can a triggered ability substitute. The `if` op's condition language CAN count permanents -- `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"controller": "you"}}, "right": {"const": 10}}` is well-formed -- but every available trigger event fires on a discrete happening (`self_enters`, `permanent_enters`, `upkeep`, ...), and Ascend is not an event: a player who is at nine permanents when this creature enters and reaches ten by playing a land gets the blessing at the instant of the tenth, with no trigger of this card's having fired, and gets it during an opponent's turn just as readily. A trigger-plus-counter version would also be a DIFFERENT card in the direction that matters, since the blessing is never lost and a re-checked trigger would come and go. The seven player-wide statics (`effect: "extra_land_drops"`, `no_hand_limit`, `play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`, `double_land_triggers`, `double_land_mana`, `freeze_opponent_lands`, `docs/card-dsl.md` "Player-wide statics") are the only things in the DSL that describe a player rather than a characteristic, and each is an unconditional permission read live off the battlefield for as long as its source is there -- none of them SETS anything, and all of them stop when the source leaves, which is the opposite of "for the rest of the game"

needs.what: an "as long as..." condition on a static ability that may read something other than counters on its own source -- here, a player-level predicate ("as long as you have the city's blessing"), so that `{"kind": "static", "effect": "grant_keyword", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "keywords": ["flying"]}` can switch on and off with the blessing. Whatever form it takes must declare its place in the fixed-order characteristics pipeline; a player-level predicate is actually the EASY case for that, since the blessing is player state rather than a derived characteristic and so cannot make one static depend on another static's output
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `_validate_static_condition` (`src/automtg/cards/loader.py:504-524`) raises `DslError` on any static `condition` whose key set is not exactly `{"counters"}`, and within that the only permitted keys are `counter`, `amount` and `op` -- i.e. the one question "how many counters of this kind sit on my own source". `docs/card-dsl.md` ("As long as...") states the same limit and its reason. "You have the city's blessing" is not a counter and is not on this permanent, so there is no spelling of this condition that loads. The richer condition language (`cmp`, `all`, `any`, `not`, `exists`, `zone_is`, `is_your_turn`) belongs to the `if` OP and is unreachable from a static: ops run inside `spell_effects` or an ability's `effects`, and a static ability has neither -- its parameters are flattened onto the ability and the characteristics pipeline never runs the effect interpreter. Granting the keyword from a trigger is not a substitute either: `grant_keyword` as an effect is an until-end-of-turn grant on a discrete event, whereas the printed line is a permanent conditional characteristic that must be true the moment the blessing is gained, including mid-combat and on an opponent's turn. Note this item is blocked SECOND, behind `ascend` above -- even with the condition language widened there is currently no blessing for it to ask about, and even with the blessing implemented this static could not consult it
